Second register source for the 2026 merger: https://www.northdata.com/Myrcotech%20AG,%20Baar/CHE-312.442.524. Judge: if the Myrcotech merger is read as a takeover, status would be acquired (2026-05); I read it as the same business under a new holding. Seat was Dübendorf until it moved to Zurich.

redeon-inc.status_detail: Merged with BioValve Technologies, Inc. in July 2001; the firm's own exit list records it as a trade sale ('Merger with BioValve Technologies, Inc.', 2001-07). Wikipedia's article on co-founder Mark Prausnitz lists 'Redeon (acquired by BioValve Technologies)'.

valuation.basis: No figure of any kind on record.

redeon-inc.notes: What Earlybird financed: Redeon itself, before the merger. The only records are the firm's own: the release of 05.02.2002 lists 'Redeon (merged with Biovalve)' among Earlybird's life-sciences portfolio companies, and the exit list dates the merger July 2001. So Earlybird was a Redeon shareholder that came into BioValve through the merger, not the other way round (no sale_consideration flag for this row; a BioValve row would carry it). Redeon was a drug-delivery start-up co-founded by the Georgia Tech microneedle researcher Mark Prausnitz (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Prausnitz); the Georgia Tech microneedle patents were assigned from BioValve Technologies to Valeritas LLC in 2006 (Google Patents US6743211). No press release, filing or article naming a round, an amount or a date was found: news.py (Bing and Google News) returned nothing for "Redeon" BioValve, "Redeon" "BioValve", "Redeon" Earlybird or "Redeon" microneedle Earlybird, and two web searches found only a vendor page (CB Insights: HQ 124 Mount Auburn Street, Cambridge, Massachusetts; investors Earlybird and BioValve). The HQ comes from that vendor page and from nothing else. Entry is therefore null.
